subject: Positioning Regressions in Facet_Grid with yscale=free

messages.author: f6aff3ab0165e685
messages.subject: Positioning Regressions in Facet_Grid with yscale=free
parts:
This question builds on the discussion https://groups.google.com/d/topic/ggplot2/me5hL8XOxTo/discussion and any similarity to that code is purely intentional.

I want to be able to have the same relative position for the display of regression equations in facet_grid when scales="free_y".  I think the solution lies in the aes(x=, y=) call in the final line, but I am just not able to formulate it.  Apologies for my clunky dataframe setup. 
Extra credit if you can tell me how to superscript the r2 with the current code or alternative code.

SITE<-rep(c("a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","i","j"),each=9)
Season<-rep(rep(c("SP","SU","F"),each=3),10)
ISA_Pct<-rep(seq(0,0.9,0.1),each=9)
INDEX<-rep(c("Q","R","S"), 30)
OImelt2<-cbind(arrange(as.data.frame(cbind(SITE, Season,INDEX, ISA_Pct)),INDEX), c(rnorm(30,2),rnorm(30,5), rnorm(30,10)))
colnames(OImelt2)[5]<-"value"
OImelt2$ISA_Pct<-as.numeric(OImelt2$ISA_Pct)
str(OImelt2)

eqnfunc <- function(d) {   # function to fit models and build text equations 
m <- lm(value~ISA_Pct,data=d) 
c(eqn=paste( "y=",round(m$coefficients[1],1), 
             if(sign(m$coefficients[2])==-1) "-" else "+",
             abs(round(m$coefficients[2],4)),"x",sep=""," ",
            "r^2","=",format(summary(m)$r.squared, digits = 2)))
} 

labeldata <- ddply(OImelt2,INDEX~Season,eqnfunc) 

x11()
p <- ggplot(OImelt2, aes(ISA_Pct, value)) + geom_point()
p + facet_grid(INDEX ~ Season, scales = "free_y")+
    stat_smooth(method="lm",se=FALSE)+
    geom_text(data=labeldata,hjust=0, vjust=0, size=3, aes(x=1,y=1 , label=eqn))

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Positioning Regressions in Facet_Grid with yscale=free
parts:
Here's one shot at it; I had to edit a few lines of your code because
the mappings didn't add up properly (the times = part of rep() in a
few places). Also notice that I defined the data directly into a data
frame rather than cbind()ing them. There are two reasons for this:

(i) Defining objects as atomic vectors and then slurping them into a
data frame is just another way to do the equivalent of attach(), which
is no longer considered part of 'good' R programming. (This topic has
been discussed several times on R-help - check out the archives for
further information.)
(ii) cbind() coerces all of its objects to the same data type. When
you 'cbind()ed' your atomic vectors, this is why ISA_Pct was converted
to factor and why you needed to add another line of code later to
coerce it back to numeric. The approach I outline below eliminates
this practice. Moral: don't use cbind() to generate a data frame;
there are better ways to go about it. (Again, copiously discussed on
R-help.)

The code:

# Generate the data:
OI <- data.frame(SITE = rep(letters[1:10], each=9),
Season = rep(c("SP","SU","F"), each=3),
ISA_Pct = rep(seq(0, 0.9, 0.1),each = 9),
INDEX = rep(c("Q","R","S"), 30) )

library(plyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Sort by index
OI <- arrange(OI,INDEX)
# add a value column
OI <- mutate(OI, value = c(rnorm(30,2), rnorm(30,5), rnorm(30,10)))
str(OI)

# A small function to perform simple linear regression
modfun <- function(d) lm(value ~ ISA_Pct, data = d)

# Apply this function recursively by INDEX and Season,
# saving the results in a list object
modlist <- dlply(OI, .(INDEX, Season), modfun)

# Function to extract model coefficients and R^2:
# Notice that the rounding is done here...
coefun <- function(m)
{
coeff <- round(coef(m), 4)
r2 <- round(summary(m)[["r.squared"]], 2)
data.frame(b0 = coeff[1], b1 = coeff[2], r2 = r2)
}

# Apply it to each model object in the list
modsumm <- ldply(modlist, coefun)

# Two utility functions to generate string representations of
# expression objects. x is taken to be an atomic vector of
# class numeric since I am using it in apply() below.
mlabels <- function(x)
paste0("hat(y) == ", x[1], " + ", x[2], "~X")
r2label <- function(x) paste0("R^2 == ", x[3])

# Add three new variables to the summary object modsumm:
# ymin is the minimum y value for each season - I take its
# floor to add additional space for the equation of the
# fitted line and R^2
# eqn is a vector of string representations of the fitted line
# equations
# rsq is a vector of string representations of the form R^2 = value
modsumm <- mutate(modsumm,
ymin = rep(ddply(OI, .(INDEX), summarise,
floor(min(value)))[, 2], each = 3),
eqn = apply(modsumm[, 3:5], 1, mlabels),
rsq = apply(modsumm[, 3:5], 1, r2label)
)
modsumm

## Notice that I used the _numeric_ columns of modsumm (3-5)
## to generate the text strings that will later be parsed into
## mathematical expressions. This is consistent with the way
## the functions mlabels and r2label were defined.

# Plot:
ggplot(OI, aes(ISA_Pct, value)) +
geom_point() +
geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
geom_text(data = modsumm, x = 0, size = 3, hjust = 0,
aes(y = ymin, label = eqn), parse = TRUE) +
geom_text(data = modsumm, x = 0, size = 3, hjust = 0,
aes(y = ymin - 0.4, label = rsq), parse = TRUE) +

Notice that geom_text() is called twice: once for the fitted model and
again for R^2. Also notice how the data frame modsumm was generated:
it contains both variables used in facet_grid() (hence, we know which
equations go in which facets), a variable was created to vary the
y-position in each row (since you're using scales = "free_y"), and
finally, it contains two additional variables (string representations
of plotmath code) to be used for the labels. The argument parse = TRUE
in geom_text() does the necessary magic.

Does that give you what you want?

Dennis

PS: Not to be too much of a nag, but I'm not a big fan of code that
runs together, so you (and others with similar proclivities) might
find this helpful: http://stat405.had.co.nz/r-style.html
